title: Extension of a zeroed counter prefix
statement: Let $A$ be counting-sort arguments, $j\in\mathbb{N}$, and $\mu'$ an integer-valued memory map. If every counter at offset $t<j$ contains zero, then changing the counter at offset $j$ to zero makes every counter at offset $t<j+1$ contain zero.
hypotheses_covered: Every counter at offset $t<j$ contains zero
replaced:
Let $c$ be the starting cell of a counter array, let $j$ be a natural number, and let
$\mu' : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$. If $\mu'(c+t)=0$ for every natural number $t<j$,
then the function obtained from $\mu'$ by setting its value at $c+j$ to zero also
vanishes at every position $c+t$ with $t<j+1$.
